name: Oasis Voice
description: TTS and streaming STT via oasis-voice sidecar (Piper TTS + Moonshine STT on the lite tier; GPU tiers available on the hosted endpoint).
_contracts_NOTE: We intentionally do NOT declare a `contracts` block here. Declaring contracts.{speechProviders,mediaUnderstandingProviders,realtimeTranscriptionProviders} makes the loader treat this plugin as lazy/capability-triggered, and that lazy load never fires for an /app/extensions/-mounted (non-bundled) plugin — so register() never runs and the provider registries stay empty. VERIFIED 2026-05-16: adding the contracts block (even alongside `activation.onStartup: true`, which did NOT override the behavior) dropped oasis-voice from the gateway plugin tally entirely (16 plugins -> 15, no `oasis-voice plugin loaded` log line). Without contracts, register() runs eagerly at boot and registerSpeechProvider/registerMediaUnderstandingProvider/registerRealtimeTranscriptionProvider populate the runtime registries. The cost: oasis-voice is absent from the manifest-metadata registry that drives media-understanding autoPriority resolution (media-understanding/manifest-metadata.ts skips providers not in contracts.mediaUnderstandingProviders). So inbound-audio routing canNOT be left to autoPriority — it MUST be pinned explicitly via `tools.media.audio.models` in config (the runtime entrypoint does exactly this; see scripts/runtime-entrypoint.sh). Outbound TTS is likewise pinned via `messages.tts.provider`. Properly fixing the contracts-vs-eager-load conflict needs an upstream openclaw loader change and is tracked separately.

endpoint.description: Base URL of the oasis-voice HTTP server. Default: http://127.0.0.1:8731

tts_voice.description: Default TTS voice passed to oasis-voice (e.g. piper:en_GB-alan-medium). Default: piper:en_GB-alan-medium

bearer_token.description: Optional Bearer token for hosted/cloud oasis-voice endpoint (CLAW-013+). Not needed for local lite tier.
